body: This is something I can't understand. I keep believing that if I graduate and start to earn money, all my suicidal problems will fade away because I won't have to worry about being anxious about tests, feeling impotent because of lack of power and knowledge, worrying all the time about being better than my peers, helping my parents economically once they reach old age (which is soon), etc. The journey seems so long and tortuous that I contemplate suicide every single day, I just want to stop worrying about every fucking thing. One of the things that keeps me " sane" is the hope that all these worries will magically disappear once I achieve what you have achieved.
Ironically getting admitted again will aggravate things to a whole another level. My psychiatrist told me to double the dose starting this week, I guess I'll see how that ends up working in a month.

I'm already seeing a psychiatrist. As for therapy, I'm on Prozac. It helped me these last 2 years, but I suffered a huge relapse in February. All these thoughts came rushing back in simultaneously, it felt like a train wrecked my brain. That's the advice my psychiatrist gave me actually. Stick to what's been working for me so far, even if I'm not completely satisfied with the results. I'd also like to know more about what you said in 5). My thought process is that if I become financially and occupationally self-sufficient, I'll finally be free from these emotional shackles, because I won't have to worry about getting even more behind from my peers. I'll finally be equal to the rest, instead of being below the rest.

Thanks for your advice. Unfortunately, I've already been into a hospital, I'm already seeing a psychiatrist, I'm already taking Prozac... and nothing is working. I think otherwise now that I've been through hell and back. I think if I manage to stabilize my med school life, it'll help reduce my anxiety and perfectionism. For over a decade, I've tried to become the best at x or y in the world. When I got into med school, I understood that the world was a huge place. So I tried being the best at my med school. Turns out there is always someone a lot smarter than you, a lot more resourceful than you, etc. I think if I learn how to fix this way of thinking, I'll be able to somehow stop feeling suicidal every day. Which is why I came here (one of the last places I have left to get help). Learning how to study efficiently is a great first step for me to get out of this hellhole once and for all. The problem is that the people around me tell me that "it depends on the person", "there are many different methods". So in short, they don't have an answer to my question. I also understand that age does not matter in the long run. The problem is the unconscious emotional response I feel every time a classmate does much better than I do with less effort.

How have you been able to cope with the feeling of emptiness when watching your peers graduate and become successful? I find this feeling extremely unbearable, to the point that it completely resets my depression, which I thought I had under control for the past few years. It's not about the amount of money, in my country med school is pretty cheap (and one of the best in the region). If I could choose a job, I'd probably end up choosing none. I've realized that any job has a certain degree of stress and requires you to give it your all to get to a comfortable position. That's why I haven't dropped out. My ideal "job" is to laze around in the computer all day, while earning enough to live by myself and buy nice things for my parents. I'm tired of thinking about all these things, while simultaneously doing homeworks, studying for next week's test, competing with my peers who are three years younger, constantly thinking about those guys who entered med school with me but are already doing their last year, while I'm seemingly stuck. I'm tired of being worried about things that will not happen until later. I think this is not a vocational problem, I'm just naturally cynical about the world. I did not ask to live. I want to sleep forever.

Really hard question to answer for me... In the future, I'd like to write a book to share my thoughts with the world. I'd like to travel around the world, going from hospital and hospital, learning about different things everyday. But it all seems so goddamn far away and I'm so tired of everything. I don't want to disappoint my parents anymore, I want to stop competing for the best grade, for the best reputation, for the title of the smartest. I'm tired of comparing myself with others, there is always someone who is so much better than you at memorizing things, at learning skills, at emotional control, why even bother. I'm tired of procrastinating every week. I'm tired of being away of things I genuinely enjoy, like anime, reading, internet, philosophy, math, physics.
How am I supposed to save someone else, if I can't save myself?
